models_evaluated: two unnamed LLMs of different sizes (smaller and larger)

links.outcome: Output agreement across prompt paraphrases and model choices in structured extraction
links.effect: Median cross-prompt kappa 0.69 and 0.68 on three-way flags; model change reassigns dominant admission tag on close to half of notes, prompt phrasing on roughly one in eight.
links.quote: On the multi-class admission categorization, changing the model reassigns the dominant tag on close to half of all notes while changing the prompt phrasing reassigns it on roughly one in eight, and the larger model places far less mass on residual catch-all categories (44% to 26%).

unlisted_practices: Simplifying extraction schemas (collapsing three-way yes/no/not_documented to binary) to reduce cross-prompt disagreement
Auditing extraction reproducibility by varying one configuration choice at a time without human-annotated ground truth

screen.reason: The study tests the sensitivity and reproducibility of LLM extraction from clinical notes under different prompt phrasings, model choices, and schema designs as a methodology for deployment auditing.

primary.practice: prompt variation and schema design testing for reproducibility auditing
